reply:
I limited the facts to the two benefits the page prices: outpatient X-rays and diagnostic radiology. Diagnostic radiology is listed as "(e.g. MRI, CAT Scan)", which is an example list and not an exact list of services. The safest mapping is therefore `imaging.diagnostic`, which covers diagnostic radiology services other than X-rays.

For each quote I used the service name plus the cost text so it appears only once on the page. Each table row reads as a single line in the layout, so I quoted the text from the line that holds the amount. The in-network and out-of-network values sit on separate lines under the service name, and the two plan columns sit side by side. I could not read a column straight down without mixing in the other plan's text. To stay within the quoting rules, I quoted only the short pieces that appear once.

The quote "$0 - $300 copay*" appears once, so I used it without the asterisk, as "$0 - $300 copay". The same applies to "$0 - $60 copay".

The out-of-network 50% coinsurance text repeats many times on the page. I added the row name "Diagnostic radiology services" for context, but that creates a mixed quote that may not match the page text exactly. Because a wrong fact is worse than a missing one, I left out the out-of-network facts and the X-ray facts, whose quotes would repeat.

The in-network $0-$300 and $0-$60 amounts are unique, so I included those two facts.
